 Los Angeles Clippers San Antonio Spurs The San Antonio Spurs had a 12-game winning streak come to an end on Tuesday night against the Detroit Pistons, but they’re in a prime spot to start a new winning streak on Thursday.
--> The San Antonio Spurs had a 12-game winning streak come to an end on Tuesday night against the Detroit Pistons, but they’re in a prime spot to start a new winning streak on Thursday.
 San Antonio is set as a 15.5-point favorite at home against the Los Angeles Clippers and Darius Garland, who were blown out by the Utah Jazz on Tuesday. The Clippers have four wins this season, but it’s hard to see this team making the play-in tournament in a loaded Western Conference.
--> San Antonio is set as a 15.5-point favorite at home against the Los Angeles Clippers and Darius Garland, who were blown out by the Utah Jazz on Tuesday. The Clippers have four wins this season, but it’s hard to see this team making the play-in tournament in a loaded Western Conference.
 The loss to Detroit wasn’t the only bad part about Tuesday’s game for San Antonio, as Dylan Harper (hip) was injured in the fourth quarter and is listed as out for this matchup. San Antonio should be able to handle business against the Clippers regardless of Harper’s status as it looks to chase the No. 1 seed in the West.

 San Antonio has hit the UNDER in 11 of 15 games (the highest rate in the NBA) while the Clippers have hit the OVER in nine of 13 games (the highest rate in the NBA). 
--> San Antonio has hit the UNDER in 11 of 15 games (the highest rate in the NBA) while the Clippers have hit the OVER in nine of 13 games (the highest rate in the NBA). 
 Still, I think the UNDER is the play in this matchup, especially with Harper sidelined for San Antonio.

 The Spurs have fallen short of 224.5 points in four of their last five games and eight games overall heading into this matchup. They rank third in the league in defensive rating and fourth in offensive rating while playing at the seventh-slowest pace in the league.

 L.A. also ranks in the back half of the NBA in pace, and it’s just 21st in the league in offensive rating.
